PullRequest.Title: Add transient UI for /btw side questions
PullRequest.Body:

`/btw` currently opens another full chat. This change keeps the source transcript and composer in place and presents the side answer in a transient card immediately above the existing composer.

## Reviewer TL;DR

**A normal durable side chat, with a transient presentation.** The provider still owns the conversation, history, model and response. Closing removes only the card; the same backing chat remains recoverable from the session's Side Chats menu. **Open Full Chat** opens that conversation through the normal Sessions navigation path.

The feature defaults off behind `chat.agentSessions.transientSideChat` (`config.chat.agentSessions.transientSideChat` in ExP). Disabled treatment or an unavailable source host uses the existing full-chat open-and-split flow.

**Invariant:** `/btw` must not hide, replace, move, rebind, or restyle the source composer.

Rebased onto `main` at `17c5935aa72`. The history remains four dependency-ordered commits:

| Commit | Purpose | Review focus |
|---|---|---|
| `570205ea0fb` — `chat: refactor: support embedded response widgets` | Generic response-widget options, hidden-input layout, focus-local routing | Existing full-chat behavior stays the default; embedded renderers cannot shadow full surfaces |
| `41d2771964c` — `sessions: refactor: make send lifecycle explicit` | Request IDs, awaited `preserveActiveChat`, close history, provider option boundary | Concurrent and failing sends cannot affect another navigation follow |
| `2faa43c0465` — `sessions: feat: add transient side-chat presentation` | Card, rollout gate, orchestration, all entry points, accessibility and regressions | Presentation ownership, cleanup, error handling, focus and measured layout |
| `301fb9e55a9` — `agentHost: polish: skip side-chat rename round-trip` | Independent latency optimization | Rename reminder suppressed only for `SideChat` origins |

The durable architecture contract is in `src/vs/sessions/SESSIONS.md`, **Transient side questions**.

## Ownership and flow

```text
/btw, response-selection question, or workbench Ask in Side Chat
  -> create a real provider-backed side chat
  -> ISideChatOrchestrationService.prepare(...)
     -> control / no live interactive host: open and split the full side chat
     -> treatment + live host: close with skipHistory, publish transient state
  -> prepared.send(...)
     -> transient: awaited send with preserveActiveChat
     -> full: ordinary foreground send
  -> provider streams into the side-chat model
```

`ITransientSideChatService` stores resource identities, not provider facades. It resolves current session/chat state reactively and revalidates a per-source presentation ID after awaiting close. Replaced questions, deletion, facade replacement, setting disable, final-host disposal and read-only transitions cannot leave a stale live card.

`ISessionsManagementService` owns provider routing and paired send-start/send-end request IDs. `ISessionsService` owns visible navigation. The `background` and `preserveActiveChat` flags never cross the provider boundary; the explicit provider field picker has a compile-time exhaustiveness guard.

Promotion and full-chat fallback verify that the requested destination became active. A late promotion result cannot delete a replacement card.

## Layout and shared widget integration

The variable-height card is an **in-flow child of `ChatInputPart`**, after the floating status-pill lane and before banners/the original composer. It does not use the fixed-height floating lane or inherit that lane's pointer-event behavior.

The nested `ChatWidget` renders response rows only, with no header/footer, follow-ups, pet or go-to-bottom control, and no visible nested composer. It is created lazily; model loads are identity/cancellation guarded; dismissal releases the widget, model reference, listeners and scheduled layout.

`isEmbedded` provides focus-local action routing while excluding the renderer from full-widget discovery. Event-driven consumers use `lastFocusedChatSurface`. Embedded widgets inherit the enclosing surface's Find support, so Cmd/Ctrl+F continues working from the answer. Both Sessions and workbench Agent Host pills explicitly publish persistent-content visibility, including when the input is read-only.

Layout is frame-coalesced and skips unchanged dimensions. Short answers stay compact; long answers are capped at **60% of the source view**, including the fractional header height, divider and outer borders. Scrolling remains inside the answer. Auto routing metadata is hidden only inside transient cards; the ordinary full chat still shows it.

## Failure handling and accessibility

`FailedAndPresented` means a live card owns the send failure. Dismissed or promoting cards decline that ownership, allowing normal caller notification instead of losing the error during promotion. Failure details are retained if promotion itself fails.

The card is a labelled region described by its question and visible status. Announcements are transition-based. Escape dismisses a pending or completed card, but yields to code-editor selections, suggestion UI and hover. From the source input it additionally yields to active requests, dictation, editing and confirmation interactions. Close returns source focus; successful promotion focuses the full-chat destination.

## Review and verification

Opus 5 maximum-reasoning reviews covered Sessions presentation, lifecycle/orchestration, shared workbench behavior and latest-main integration. Findings were fixed and re-reviewed. The OSS run then exposed routing metadata and border-budget regressions; those were fixed, regression-covered, re-reviewed, and the entire live flow was repeated.

Current validation:

- Complete development build via `npm run build-fast`; client type check and changed-file ESLint/Stylelint pass.
- **283 focused Electron tests pass** (2 existing pending), including send/promotion races, read-only pill visibility, real fractional-header/border measurement, metadata scoping, source input, Find and side-chat entry points.
- **44 Agent Host title tests pass**.
- **Ten authenticated, provider-backed Code OSS scenarios pass on the final rebased build**: source context/composer identity and styling; Find from the card; draft preservation; strict height cap; internal wheel scrolling; code-selection Escape; promotion; pending-card dismissal; selected-response questions; and live setting disable/full-chat fallback.
- Measured long-answer geometry: **524.40625px card in an 876px source view**, below the **525.6px cap**, with **1,410px** scroll extent in a **467px** response viewport.

Screenshots, a Playwright trace, assertion results and a 59-second recording were retained with the session's OSS evidence report.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Active-agent title handling put an awaited session-database metadata read and a mandatory rename_chat tool instruction on outgoing turns for independent side chats, adding I/O and an avoidable tool round-trip before the side answer could settle.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Agent Host side questions incurred unnecessary response latency from title metadata lookup and automatic rename-tool execution even though these transient side chats do not need a rename reminder.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Side-chat turns now return before persisted title metadata I/O and before injecting the mandatory rename_chat instruction, removing the unnecessary database read and rename tool/agent continuation from each eligible side-chat response path.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: SessionTitleContribution.onOutgoingTurn synchronously awaits prepareInstructionForAgent on every outgoing Agent Host turn. In the base revision, eligible independent chats then awaited _readPersistedTitleMetadata, which opens the session database and reads metadata, and could return CHAT_RENAME_REMINDER, an instruction explicitly requiring the agent to invoke rename_chat. The added SideChat-origin guard at RIGHT line 519 exits before both operations; the added test seeds an automatic side-chat title and verifies the outgoing instruction is now undefined. blame_base_line attributes the old metadata/reminder path to 274239ff17a15514f74288e0f8fb21eaccce599b.

Scenarios.Scenario: Ask a `/btw` or selection side question with transient presentation enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Provider-backed side-chat creation and local close/presentation must complete before the caller starts the awaited send. The nested model acquisition starts reactively after presentation and is off the send critical path; the provider send remains the answer critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create a provider-backed side chat through ISessionsManagementService/createSideChatInSession.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider creation per submitted side question; no per-turn or per-row fan-out beyond the single branch operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior `/btw` flow performed the same single provider-backed side-chat creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before transient state can be published and before sending.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: On a cold cache, resolve/load the remote chat session through IChatService.acquireOrLoadSession; on a warm cache, acquire the existing model reference.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one load per currently presented side-chat identity; replacement cancels the prior load and dismissal releases the reference.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior full-chat presentation also needed a ChatWidget model acquisition for the newly opened side chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the send critical path; it controls when response content can render in the card.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the single request through the selected sessions provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider send per submitted question, including superseded presentations, matching the prior durable-chat behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior flow sent one provider request after opening the full side chat.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of submitted side questions and provider response size. Each source retains at most one live card/model; durable closed-chat membership grows with the session's side-chat catalog, adding linear local set/filter work but no new per-item external calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Creation and presentation are sequential. Cold nested model acquisition can overlap the subsequent provider send. Presentation ownership is coalesced per source chat with cancellation tokens; older sends may still settle independently, preserving existing send semantics.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold cards call the existing remote-session resolver once; warm models are reference-counted and reused. There is no negative cache, but failed or cancelled identities are removed and a replacement gets a fresh guarded load.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: create, close, model-load, send, cancellation, and disposal paths are directly traced in changed code and focused tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider latency and unusually long-lived sessions vary, but boundary cardinality is unchanged from the prior full-chat path and live presentation resources are bounded per source.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The changed presentation avoids full navigation, does not multiply provider calls, loads the model lazily, and releases/cancels card resources on dismissal or replacement.

Scenarios.Scenario: Ask a side question when the experiment is disabled or no live source host exists
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Provider creation, fallback chat open/session resolution, split, then provider send are sequential; the open must become active before send proceeds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One provider creation occurred before every prior full-chat side question.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve/load the destination session if needed while opening the side chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one open resolution per question; cancelled stale opens do not activate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old helper also awaited openChat before splitting and sending.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks send so the destination is verified active.

ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One provider send occurred in the prior full-chat flow.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Submitted questions; external boundary count remains constant per question.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A per-source presentation token cancels stale opens. The fallback itself is serialized create -> open -> send, matching the old flow.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm sessions/models avoid remote restoration; cold opens use existing session/model caches. The disabled path checks configuration before closing or constructing a nested ChatWidget.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact provider/open latency varies, but before/after operation count and ordering are established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: fallback adds only lightweight presentation bookkeeping and preserves the previous external boundary count and ordering.

Scenarios.Scenario: Stream and lay out a transient side-chat answer
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Streaming model updates render into one embedded ChatWidget. Content-height changes schedule one next-animation-frame measurement/layout; unchanged dimensions skip nested layout.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Response content parts and animation frames while content height changes. Height is capped at 60% of the source view and only one live card exists per source.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Refresh requests are coalesced by a single scheduled animation-frame disposable. Rendering remains on the UI thread, with at most one refresh callback pending per card.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Rendered activity plaintext is WeakMap-cached by markdown object/value. Widget/model construction is lazy on first live state and the widget is disposed when state clears.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for UI scheduling and cleanup; moderate for extreme response-size prevalence.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very tool-heavy responses can increase content scans, but reverse scans usually terminate at the latest activity and geometry work is frame-bounded; no evidence supports user-visible regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The diff explicitly coalesces geometry work, avoids unchanged nested layouts, caps the viewport, and disposes scheduled work and the nested widget.

Scenarios.Scenario: Dismiss, replace, or promote a transient card
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Dismissal is local and immediate. Replacement cancels old presentation/model ownership. Promotion performs one normal openChat and verifies active destination before removing state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open/resolve the durable side chat through the normal Sessions navigation path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One open per explicit promotion action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no transient promotion action; the old side chat was already open as a full chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks successful promotion/focus, but not the already streaming transient answer.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: User promotion/dismissal actions and replacement frequency; retained live resources stay bounded to one card per source.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Monotonic per-source cancellation tokens guard close/open races. Model load cancellation and identity checks prevent stale references; promotion and replacement revalidate ownership after awaits.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Promotion uses normal session caches. Dismissal clears the model reference and widget; replacement cancels the prior load rather than retaining both.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote promotion latency depends on provider/cache state, but it is user-requested and occurs once.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: the only new boundary is explicitly requested promotion, while cleanup and stale-operation cancellation are complete.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open ordinary Sessions chat views while transient side chat is unused
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ChatView constructs lightweight hidden card chrome and host registration, but nested ChatWidget construction and model/network loading do not occur until a transient state exists.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of concurrently instantiated ChatViews; each adds fixed DOM/context/listener overhead.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No asynchronous model work starts without a live card.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No model cache is touched. The delayed singleton service and per-view host are disposed with their owners.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the eager fixed allocation, low for any material user-visible impact.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The fixed eager chrome cost is small and visible-view cardinality is bounded by the session grid; no measured or code-evidenced startup impact justifies a finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding because the added unused-feature overhead is fixed and lightweight, while all heavyweight renderer/model work remains lazy.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send an Agent Host side-chat turn with active-agent title generation enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SessionTitleContribution.onOutgoingTurn awaits title instruction preparation before outgoing turn assembly. The added SideChat guard now exits before persisted metadata access and before injecting a mandatory rename_chat instruction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the session database and read title-source metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously one read for each eligible outgoing side-chat turn until renamed; now zero for SideChat origins.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The base revision awaited this metadata read for independent side chats.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Previously blocked outgoing-turn preparation; removed by the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Inject a mandatory rename_chat instruction that can require a tool invocation and agent continuation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously one rename instruction for an eligible automatically titled side chat; now none for SideChat origins.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The base path returned CHAT_RENAME_REMINDER for eligible side chats.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Previously added avoidable tool/continuation latency to the side answer; removed by the diff.

Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Sequential on the outgoing-turn contribution path; one title preparation per outgoing turn.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The old metadata path was not cached for this decision except after rename state became known; the new origin check bypasses it deterministically.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High; the fixing line, caller, boundary, test, and introducing commit are all traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact tool continuation latency varies by provider, but the removed database and mandatory tool mechanisms are directly established.
Scenarios.Verdict: This PR fixes a concrete latency regression; it was recorded with report_regression_fix and is not a review finding.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 67 changed patches. Traced transient creation/send/fallback, cold and warm model acquisition, streaming layout, lifecycle cleanup, promotion, ordinary view construction, closed-chat scaling, and Agent Host title handling. No actionable performance regression introduced by the diff met the reporting threshold. Recorded one concrete regression fix for unnecessary side-chat title metadata I/O and rename-tool work.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
